title: A remote install can silently do nothing - the engine dep filter drops every dep and the POST still answers success
description:
SURFACED 2026-08-09 during MPI-450's throwaway-Pod session, which lost two Pod legs to it before the cause was found.

POST /comfy/models/download/start runs its dependencies through _filterDepsForEngine(modelId, dependencies, 'remote'|'local') (routes/downloadManager.js), which intersects the request against the model's universe for THAT engine. That filter is correct and deliberate - MPI-163/179 added it so a stale client cannot install the wrong engine's files. The defect is what happens when it removes EVERYTHING: the route carries on, creates or reuses the model job with an empty dep set, and returns {success: true} with a job reporting 0/0 bytes that settles straight to 'complete'. No dep is installed, no error is raised, nothing is logged at warn level, and the caller is told it worked.

MEASURED, twice, on a live CPU download Pod:
  1. dependencies sent as ID STRINGS rather than dep OBJECTS -> filtered to nothing -> {success:true}, job ltx-23 'complete' 0/0. Nothing downloaded.
  2. ltx23-transformer-int8 requested against model ltx-23 -> that transformer belongs to the BALANCED tier, so the remote universe for ltx-23 excludes it -> filtered to nothing -> {success:true} again, and a Pod was deleted mid-'download' that had never started.

WHO CAN HIT IT: any caller that is not the renderer's own resolver - scripts/smoke-workflows.mjs, an agent driving the API, a stale client after a model's dep set is re-tiered, or a future flow that composes a dep list by hand. The renderer resolves per-engine correctly today, so this is not a reported user bug; it is a silent-failure class that turns a wrong request into a fake success rather than a diagnosable error.

NOT A 1.4 GATE: pre-existing, not a regression, and no user path reaches it. Recorded so it is not rediscovered by the next person who loses an afternoon to it.

FIX DIRECTION (decide, do not assume): when the filter empties a non-empty request, that is a caller error, not a no-op. Answer 422 with the dropped ids and the engine that rejected them, or at minimum log a warn naming them and mark the job errored rather than complete. Whatever the shape, a request to install something must never report success having installed nothing. Check BOTH engine paths - the local branch at routes/downloadManager.js:1575 does the same filtering and has the same hole - and check the uninstall route too (MPI-276 G13 gave it the same filter, so an uninstall can equally report success having deleted nothing).
